Horayot 4b:1.english: Further regarding a court ruling that involves uprooting a mitzva, Rav Yosef raises a dilemma: If the court issued a ruling that there is no prohibition against plowing on Shabbat, what is the halakha? The Gemara elaborates: Do we say that since the judges agree to the application of the entire matter of prohibitions on Shabbat and their ruling is exclusively with regard to plowing, its status is tantamount to nullification of a portion of the mitzva and fulfillment of a portion of the mitzva? Or perhaps, since the judges are abolishing the principal category of labor of plowing in its entirety, it is tantamount to abolishing the essence of the mitzva of Shabbat.

Horayot 4b:11.hebrew: מתני׳ הורו ב"ד וידע אחד מהן שטעו ואמר להן טועין אתם או שלא היה מופלא של ב"ד שם או שהיה אחד מהן גר או ממזר או נתין או זקן שלא ראוי לבנים ה"ז פטור שנאמ' כאן עדה ונאמר להלן עדה מה עדה האמורה להלן כולן ראוין להוראה אף עדה האמורה כאן עד שיהיו כולן ראוין להוראה:
Horayot 4b:11.english: MISHNA: If the court issued a ruling, and one of the judges knew that they erred and he said to them: You are mistaken; or if the most distinguished [mufla] member of the court was not there for that session of the Sanhedrin, or if one of the judges was disqualified from serving as a judge, e.g., because he was a convert, or a child born from an incestuous or adulterous relationship [mamzer], or a Gibeonite, or an old man no longer able to father children, this court is exempt, because they have not rendered a full-fledged ruling. This is derived by means of a verbal analogy, as “assembly” is stated here with regard to a court that issues an erroneous ruling: “And if the entire assembly of Israel shall act unwittingly” (Leviticus 4:13), and “assembly” is stated there with regard to the halakha of one who commits murder unwittingly: “And the assembly shall judge between the one who struck and the blood redeemer” (Numbers 35:24). Just as in the “assembly” stated there, with regard to the unwitting murderer, all the judges must be fit to issue rulings, so too, in the “assembly” stated here, with regard to the court that issued an erroneous ruling; the court will not be liable unless all the judges will be fit to issue rulings.

Horayot 4b:13.english: GEMARA: The Mishnah teaches: Or if the mufla of the court was not there, the court is exempt. From where do we derive this halakha? Rav Sheshet said, and likewise the Sage of the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught: For what reason did the Sages of the Mishnah say: If the court issued a ruling with regard to a matter with which the Sadducees agree, the judges are exempt? It is due to the fact that judges of such a court are not considered fit to issue rulings, since it was incumbent upon them to learn that halakha that is written explicitly in the Torah, and they did not learn it. Similarly, in a case where the mufla of the court was not there, the judges are also exempt, as it was incumbent upon them to learn and they did not learn.

Horayot 4b:14.english: We further learned in the Mishnah: “Assembly” is stated there and “assembly” is stated here… the court will not be liable unless all the judges will be fit to issue rulings. And the Gemara asks: And there, from where do we derive that all of them must be fit to issue rulings? And the Gemara answers: This is as Rav Ḥisda says that the verse states concerning the appointment of the seventy Elders by Moses: “That they may stand there with you” (Numbers 11:16), to say that “with you” means: Similar to you, Moses, in the sense that they must all be fit to issue rulings.

Horayot 4b:15.english: And they ask: And say that “with you” means that they shall be fit for the Divine Presence, and the verse intends to say that they should stand together to receive the Divine Presence! Rather, Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak says: We learn that all of them must be fit to issue rulings from what the verse states concerning the judges whom Moses appointed: “And they shall judge the people at all times…and ease your burden from upon you and bear it with you” (Exodus 18:22), meaning that “with you” signifies: Similar to you.

Horayot 4b:17.english: GEMARA: The mishna teaches: If the court issued the erroneous ruling unwittingly and the congregation performed a transgression intentionally, these people are exempt. The Gemara infers: But if the person performed a transgression unwittingly in a manner similar to that of an intentional transgression, the person is liable. And what are the circumstances of that performance? It is a case where the court issued a ruling that forbidden fat is permitted, and the forbidden fat became confused for a person with permitted fat and he ate the forbidden fat.

Horayot 4b:19.english: MISHNA: If the judges of the court issued an erroneous ruling and the entire congregation or a majority thereof performed a transgression on the basis of their ruling, the judges bring a bull as an unwitting communal sin-offering. And if the erroneous ruling involved idol worship, the judges bring a bull and a goat, as it is written in the Torah (see Numbers 15:24); this is the statement of Rabbi Meir. Rabbi Yehuda says: It is not the court that brings the offering, it is the people. Twelve tribes that sinned bring twelve bulls, i.e., each tribe brings one, and for idol worship they bring twelve bulls and twelve goats, as each tribe is a congregation.

Horayot 5a:1.english: Rabbi Shimon says: They bring thirteen bulls, which are one bull for each and every tribe and one bull for the court; **and for idol worship they bring thirteen bulls and thirteen goats,** which are **a bull and a goat for each and every tribe and a bull and a goat for** the **court.**

Horayot 5a:2:1.hebrew: הורו בית דין ועשו שבעה שבטים או רובו - של כל שבט ושבט דשבעה שבטים, וכגון שהיו רובן של ישראל, מביאין פר וכו', דברי רבי מאיר [דסבירא ליה] בית דין מביאין פר ולא ציבור:

Horayot 5a:2:2.hebrew: רבי יהודה אומר ז' שבטים שחטאו מביאין ז' פרים ושאר שבטים שלא חטאו מביאין פר פר על ידיהם - כלומר: פר לכל שבט ושבט. ואמר בגמרא שז' שאמר ר' יהודה לאו דווקא, דהוא הדין לשבט אחד שחטא על הוראת בית דין הגדול, שהשאר שבטים שלא חטאו מביאין על ידיהן פר פר. ואיידי שאמר ר"מ ז', שהוא צריך רובא ממש, אמר ר' יהודה נמי:

Horayot 5a:3.english: If the court of one of the tribes issued a ruling and that tribe performed a transgression on the basis of its ruling, that tribe is liable to bring an offering and the rest of all the tribes are exempt; this is the statement of Rabbi Yehuda. And the Rabbis say: One is liable to bring an offering for an unwitting communal sin only for rulings of the High Court alone, as it is stated: “And if the entire assembly of Israel shall act unwittingly” (Leviticus 4:13), to teach us that there is liability specifically for a ruling of the assembly, i.e., the court, of the entire people, but not for a ruling of **the assembly of that** particular **tribe,** as that is not the assembly of all Israel.

Rashi on Horayot 4b:10:1.english: A prophet who prophesies - For example, one who was initially a true prophet and eventually became a false prophet, who prophesied to uproot a matter from the words of the Torah, is liable, and everyone agrees to strangulation.

Rashi on Horayot 4b:10:2.hebrew: לקיום מקצת ולבטל מקצת - דשאר מצות רבי שמעון פוטר, והוא הדין לרבנן:

Rashi on Horayot 4b:10:3.hebrew: ובעבודת כוכבים אפילו אמר לך היום עובדה ולמחר בטלה - דהיינו קיום מקצת וביטול מקצת דעבודת כוכבים חייב, דרחמנא אמר: להדיחך מן הדרך, אפילו מקצת דרך, ובעבודת כוכבים הוא דכתיב. וכי קתני חייב, כגון לרבנן בסקילה ולרבי שמעון בחנק. והכי מתרץ ליה רב חסדא בפרק אלו הן הנחנקין (סנהדרין דף צ.). והיום עובדה ולמחר בטלה כאין שבת בשביעית דמי, וקרי להו ביטול מקצת וקיום מקצת. שמע מינה:

Rashi on Horayot 4b:11:1.hebrew: ואמר להם טועים אתם - לא הוי הוראה מעליא ופטור, דבעינן עד שיורו כולן כדאמר לעיל:
Rashi on Horayot 4b:11:1.english: And he said to them: You are mistaken - This is not considered a proper ruling, and they are exempt, because we require that all of them issue the ruling, as stated above.

Rashi on Horayot 4b:11:2.hebrew: או שלא היה מופלא של ב"ד שם - אף על גב דלא הוה מסנהדרין עצמן, דאילו הוי מסנהדרין עצמן, אפילו (אם) קטן שבכולן לא היה שם, לא הויא הוראה מעליא, כדאמר לקמן מאם כל עדת איתא לכולה סנהדרי הויא הוראה ואי לא לא. ואיכא למימר: נצטרך אחד מהן לצאת לדרך ומינו אחר במקומו, או נמי זקן (או) שאין לו בנים היה, לכך נתמנה אחר בסנהדרין:
Rashi on Horayot 4b:11:2.english: Or if the most distinguished member of the court was not there - Even though he was not from the Sanhedrin members themselves, for if he was from the Sanhedrin members themselves, even if the youngest among them was not there, it would not be a proper ruling, as it says later from 'if the entire assembly' that the entire Sanhedrin must be present for it to be a ruling, and if not, then not. And one might say: One of them needed to go on a journey and they appointed another in his place; or alternatively, he was an old man who had no children, and therefore another was appointed to the Sanhedrin.

Rashi on Horayot 4b:11:3.hebrew: או זקן שאין ראוי לבנים - וקשיא לי: מפני מה אין ראוי להוראה:
Rashi on Horayot 4b:11:3.english: Or an old man no longer able to father children - And it is difficult for me: Why is he not fit to issue rulings?

Rashi on Horayot 4b:14:1.english: And there, from where do we derive it? - that all of them must be fit to issue rulings.

Rashi on Horayot 4b:14:2.hebrew: אמר רב חסדא - גמר ממשה; דמשה אוקי סנהדרין דהוו כולן ראויין להוראה, דכתיב: והתיצבו שם עמך, עמך בדומין לך, דליהוי (הם) כולן ראויין להוראה. ה"נ בעינן דסנהדרי דעלמא ליהוו ראויין להוראה. והואיל ומצינו דעדה האמורה כאן כולן ראויין להוראה, שמעינן מינה נמי דהיינו סנהדרי גדולה, דתניא בת"כ: עדת ישראל עדה המיוחדת לכל ישראל, ואיזו זו — סנהדרי גדולה:
Rashi on Horayot 4b:14:2.english: Rav Ḥisda says - He derives it from Moses; for Moses established a Sanhedrin where all its members were fit to issue rulings, as it is written: “And they shall stand there with you,” meaning “with you” in the sense of “similar to you,” that they should all be fit to issue rulings. So too, we require that the Sanhedrin in general should be fit to issue rulings. And since we find that the “assembly” mentioned here refers to judges all of whom are fit to issue rulings, we also learn from it that this refers to the Great Sanhedrin, as it is taught in Torat Kohanim: “Assembly of Israel” refers to an assembly unique to all of Israel, and which is this? The Great Sanhedrin.

Rashi on Horayot 4b:15:1.hebrew: ואימא עמך משום שכינה - דלגופיה הוא דאתא, כלומר: שיהו עומדין עמך ולא יכנסו לפני ולפנים במקום שכינה, דסלקא דעתא אמינא: והואיל דכתב אספה לי, דיכנסו במקום שכינה. קא משמע לן [לשון אחר]: עמך משום שכינה, כלומר: ברור צדיקים גמורים שאני רוצה להשרות שכינה עליהם:
Rashi on Horayot 4b:15:1.english: And say that “with you” is for the Divine Presence - for it came for its own sake, meaning: that they should stand with you and not enter before the innermost part, in the place of the Divine Presence. For one might have thought, since it is written “Gather for Me,” that they should enter the place of the Divine Presence. This comes to teach us. [Another explanation]: “With you” is for the Divine Presence, meaning: choose perfectly righteous people upon whom I wish to cause My Divine Presence to rest.

Rashi on Horayot 4b:15:2.english: With you, similar to you - that they should be fit to issue rulings.

Rashi on Horayot 4b:16:1.hebrew: הורו בית דין שוגגין ועשו הקהל שוגגין - על פיהם, בית דין מביאין פר. רבי מאיר כדאית ליה, ורבי יהודה כדאית ליה, ורבי שמעון כדאית ליה, דהוי הוראה מעליא:
Rashi on Horayot 4b:16:1.english: If the court issued an unwitting ruling and the congregation performed unwittingly - based on their ruling, the court brings a bull. Rabbi Meir holds his view, and Rabbi Yehuda holds his view, and Rabbi Shimon holds his view, that this constitutes a proper ruling.

Rashi on Horayot 4b:16:2.hebrew: הורו בית דין מזידין ועשו הקהל שוגגין - לא הוי הוראה מעליא, ד'אם כל עדת ישראל ישגו' כתיב, דבעינן שוגגין בבית דין. והכא הוה ליה שגגת מעשה בלא הוראה, ומביאין כל אחד מן הקהל כשבה או שעירה, דכיחיד דמו:
Rashi on Horayot 4b:16:2.english: If the court issued an intentional ruling and the congregation performed unwittingly - this is not a proper ruling, as it is written 'If the entire assembly of Israel shall act unwittingly,' which requires the court to be unwitting. Here, it is an unwitting action without a ruling, and each member of the congregation brings a female lamb or a female goat, for they are considered like an individual.

Rashi on Horayot 4b:16:3.hebrew: הורו בית דין שוגגין ועשו הקהל מזידים פטורים - דמזיד לאו בר קרבן הוא:
Rashi on Horayot 4b:16:3.english: If the court issued an unwitting ruling and the congregation performed intentionally, they are exempt - because one who acts intentionally is not subject to an offering.

Rashi on Horayot 4b:17:1.hebrew: טעמא דשוגגין ועשו מזידים דפטורין - דמזיד לאו בר קרבן הוא, לא צבור ולא יחיד. הא שוגג דומיא דמזיד דלא הוי ממש תולה בב"ד, הוי שוגג תולה בעצמו וחייב בשגגת מעשה קרינא ביה:
Rashi on Horayot 4b:17:1.english: The reason that if they erred unwittingly and acted intentionally, they are exempt - is because an intentional act does not warrant a sacrifice, neither for the community nor for an individual. But if one erred unwittingly in a manner similar to an intentional act, where it is not truly attributed to the court, then it is an unwitting act attributed to himself, and he is liable for a sin of action.

Rashi on Horayot 4b:17:2.hebrew: כגון שהורו ב"ד שחלב מותר - שעל הקרב ולא שעל הכליות, דלא הוי עוקר כל הגוף:
Rashi on Horayot 4b:17:2.english: For example, where the court ruled that forbidden fat is permitted - referring to the fat on the entrails, not the fat on the kidneys, as that would not be uprooting the entire body of the Torah.

Rashi on Horayot 4b:17:3.hebrew: ונתחלף חלב בשומן ואכלו - דחייב דתולה בעצמו הוא. והאי דקרי ליה דומיא דמזיד משום דכי היכי דמזיד לאו תולה בב"ד הוא, האי שוגג נמי לאו תולה בב"ד הוא, ותפשוט האי דבעי רמי בר חמא (לעיל הוריות דף ב):
Rashi on Horayot 4b:17:3.english: And he confused forbidden fat with permitted fat and ate it - for he is liable, as he attributes the error to himself. And this is called 'similar to an intentional act' because just as an intentional act is not attributed to the court, so too this unwitting act is not attributed to the court. And this would resolve the dilemma that Rami bar Ḥama raised (above, Horayot page 2).

Rashi on Horayot 4b:18:1.hebrew: אמר לך - רמי בר חמא: האי דקתני שוגגין ועשו מזידים לאו למידק מינה קא אתי, אלא איידי דתנא מזידין ועשו שוגגין, תנא נמי שוגגין ועשו מזידים, וכדי נסבה ולא דייקי' מינה כלום, ובעיא דידי' מהא ליכא למשמע מינה:
Rashi on Horayot 4b:18:1.english: He could say to you - Rami bar Ḥama: This which the Mishna teaches, 'unwittingly and acted intentionally,' is not meant for inference, but rather since the *tanna* taught 'intentionally and acted unwittingly,' he also taught 'unwittingly and acted intentionally,' and it is merely a stylistic parallel, and we do not infer anything from it, and my dilemma cannot be resolved from this.

Rashi on Horayot 4b:19:1.english: If the court issued a ruling and the entire congregation or a majority thereof performed on its basis, they bring a bull - for example, the court brings the offering, and not the public.

Rashi on Horayot 4b:19:2.english: For idol worship, the court brings a bull and a goat; this is the statement of Rabbi Meir - because for idol worship, when there is an erroneous ruling, they bring a bull and a goat. As it is written in the portion of Shelach Lecha: 'And if you err and do not perform all these commandments' (Numbers 15:22), which refers to idol worship, as it states later in the chapter 'Hora Kohen Mashiach': 'Which commandment is equivalent to all the commandments? You must say: This is idol worship.' And it is written (Numbers 15:24): 'And the entire congregation shall offer one bull from the herd as a burnt offering for a pleasing aroma to the Lord, with its meal offering and its libation according to the ordinance, and one he-goat for a sin offering.'

Rashi on Horayot 4b:19:3.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: Twelve tribes bring twelve bulls - because each and every tribe is called a congregation, and he holds that the public brings a bull, not the court.

Rashi on Horayot 4b:1:1.english: Rav Yosef raises a dilemma: There is no plowing on Shabbat, what is it? - Here, Rav Yosef's dilemma is not concerning a matter that the Sadducees do not agree with at all; rather, his dilemma is regarding nullification of a portion and fulfillment of a portion.

Rashi on Horayot 4b:1:2.hebrew: מי אמרינן כיון דקא מודו - בית דין בכולהו שאר מלאכות דשבת דאסירי, כביטול מקצת וקיום מקצת דמי וחייבין:

Rashi on Horayot 4b:3:1.english: (And all of them) as we explained - Above, that it is not considered uprooting the entire essence of the *shomeret yom* (woman who observes a day for a day).

Rashi on Horayot 4b:5:1.english: (And all of it) as we explained - That passing and throwing are permitted, as it is not considered uprooting the entire essence.

Rashi on Horayot 4b:7:1.english: (And all of it) as we explained - That bowing in an atypical manner is permitted.

Rashi on Horayot 4b:8:1.english: In plowing and in harvest you shall rest - Which implies: During a time when there is plowing, meaning in the other years of the Sabbatical cycle, there is Shabbat.

Rashi on Horayot 4b:8:2.english: During a time when there is no plowing - Meaning, in the Sabbatical Year, there is no Shabbat.

Rashi on Horayot 5a:1:1.english: Rabbi Shimon says: Thirteen bulls - one bull for each and every tribe and one bull for the court. And the reasoning for all of them is explained in the Gemara.

Rashi on Horayot 5a:2:1.english: If the court issued a ruling and seven tribes or a majority thereof performed - a majority of each and every one of the seven tribes, and for example, they constituted a majority of Israel, they bring a bull, etc.; these are the words of Rabbi Meir, who holds that the court brings a bull and not the public.

Rashi on Horayot 5a:2:2.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: Seven tribes that sinned bring seven bulls, and the rest of the tribes that did not sin bring one bull each on their behalf - meaning, one bull for each and every tribe. And it is stated in the Gemara that the 'seven' that Rabbi Yehuda mentioned is not precise, for the same applies to one tribe that sinned based on the ruling of the High Court, that the rest of the tribes that did not sin bring one bull each on their behalf. And since Rabbi Meir mentioned 'seven' because he requires an actual majority, Rabbi Yehuda also mentioned 'seven'.

Rashi on Horayot 5a:3:1.english: And the Rabbis say: They are liable to bring a bull only for a ruling of the High Court - but a single tribe acting on the ruling of its own court is considered like an unwitting action, and each person brings a female lamb or a female goat.

Rashi on Horayot 5a:3:2.english: The assembly of Israel - this refers to the Sanhedrin, meaning the Sanhedrin of Israel, which is the High Court.

Steinsaltz comment #1 on Horayot 4b:1.english:
Rashi wrote that this dilemma of Rav Yosef is not a continuation of the previous discussion, but rather a question in itself: If a court ruled to permit one of the labors of Shabbat entirely, is it considered ruling on a portion or nullifying an entire matter?

However, the commentators raise another question: The labor of plowing is explicitly forbidden in the Torah (as it says, "In plowing and in harvest you shall rest"), and therefore it is a matter that the Sadducees agree with, and according to Shmuel, this is not a valid ruling! Tosafot said that regarding plowing itself, Rav Yosef knows that this is not a valid ruling, but he mentioned plowing as an example of one of the labors of Shabbat, and he chose this example because it is listed first in the count of labors. Meiri writes similarly, that regarding plowing, since it is explicit in the Torah, it is certainly not a valid ruling. Indeed, the Rosh believes that Rav Yosef does not accept Shmuel's opinion, and therefore his question is only a continuation of the Mishnah: Is this matter called a partial mitzva or a complete mitzva (and Chafetz Hashem also inclined to this view, and others). Whereas the Rama (cited in the Rosh) believes that even regarding the labor of plowing, the Sadducees do not agree, because they interpret the verse "In plowing and in harvest you shall rest" not as a prohibition on these labors, but "plowing" and "harvest" are, in their opinion, seasons of the year (winter and summer), and they interpret the verse as saying that one must rest from labor in all seasons of the year.

Steinsaltz comment #1 on Horayot 4b:11.english:
The most distinguished member of the court is the greatest of the Sages, the head of the *yeshiva*, to whom all others are like students. Generally, he is the one appointed to be the *Nasi* (president) of the Sanhedrin (Rambam).

Rashi explains (in a second explanation) that there was a complete quorum of the Sanhedrin present (for all opinions agree that if the entire Sanhedrin did not issue the ruling, it is not a valid ruling), but it happened that the most distinguished member of the court went elsewhere, and another was appointed in his place temporarily to complete the quorum (and similarly in R. Chananel, and see also in Be'er Sheva and others). However, Rashi also explains another interpretation, that the most distinguished member of the court was not counted among the members of the Sanhedrin. This is possible due to various reasons, such as this great Sage having a disqualification that prevented him from being a member of the court (e.g., he had a physical blemish, or a lineage disqualification, or he was extremely old, and so on). Yet, despite these, he is the greatest of the Sages, and everyone must learn from him. Similarly, the Ri'd wrote, bringing a kind of proof from what is mentioned, 'seventy and two elders,' implying that there was an additional Sage who was not counted among the seventy-one members of the Sanhedrin (and see in the book Margaliyot HaYam, which elaborates on this view).

Steinsaltz comment #1 on Horayot 4b:13.english: In the book Be'er Sheva, it wondered what this has to do with the mufla of the court. And in Ḥak Natan, it explains that just as in another place they should have learned and did not learn, so too here – they should have waited until the mufla of the court arrived and then ruled on this question.

Steinsaltz comment #1 on Horayot 4b:15.english: Rashi explains in one interpretation – for the sake of the Divine Presence, that they must be great men worthy for the Divine Presence to rest upon them. And in another explanation, he wrote that it comes to say that they should be with him, but not right next to him, because Moses entered the holy place to receive his prophecy, and they are forbidden to do so. And the Rosh wrote, for the sake of the Divine Presence – that they should be with him so that the Divine Presence may rest upon them.

Steinsaltz comment #1 on Horayot 4b:8.english:
Some sages believe that this question is not related to Rav Yosef's question, but is a different question (on the same topic): Is nullification for a specific time considered partial nullification (Chafetz Hashem, Magen Giborim)? And indeed, this is somewhat implied by the style of the Gemara's words.

However, the Rosh explains it differently, and it appears from his wording that he had a different version: If you were to say that there is no plowing on Shabbat, which is considered uprooting the entire essence and they are exempt, then they said: What is the law if there is no plowing or harvesting on Shabbat during the Sabbatical Year? And according to this version, the ruling of the Rambam (which many wondered about) that resolves Rav Yosef's question is understood, as he ruled according to his custom of "if you were to say."

Steinsaltz comment #2 on Horayot 4b:1.english:
If a court ruled that there is no plowing on Shabbat, they are liable to bring an offering.

See in the Kesef Mishneh and Lechem Mishneh that they labored to explain in various ways how the Rambam solved this problem which remained unresolved in the Gemara. And some wrote that the Rambam had a variant reading later in the Gemara: "Come and hear from Rabbi Zeira's dilemma," meaning that by resolving Rabbi Zeira's dilemma, Rav Yosef's dilemma was also resolved. (Rambam, Sefer Korbanot, Hilkhot Shegagot 14:2).

Steinsaltz comment #2 on Horayot 4b:11.hebrew:
ובירושלמי מסבירים שאף שאין ממנים אותם לכתחילה, מדובר כאשר עברו ומינוהו. ובפירוש אחר אמרו שלא היה ממנים הסנהדרין אבל היה עימם בזמן הדיונים.

ולעצם הענין יש שכתבו כי במקרים מיוחדים היו ממנים גם פסולים מסוג זה לסנהרין (והביאו ראיה משמעיה ואבטליון שהיו, כנראה, גרים).
Steinsaltz comment #2 on Horayot 4b:11.english:
And in the Yerushalmi, they explain that even though they are not appointed *ab initio*, it refers to a case where they transgressed and appointed him. In another explanation, they said that he was not appointed to the Sanhedrin but was with them during the deliberations.

Regarding the matter itself, some have written that in special cases, even disqualified individuals of this type were appointed to the Sanhedrin (and they brought proof from Shemaya and Avtalyon, who were, apparently, converts).

Steinsaltz comment #3 on Horayot 4b:11.hebrew: בענין גר או ממזר יש מקום לומר את שניהם, כי גר בא מטיפה פסולה, וממזר פסול לבוא בקהל, אבל לכאורה נתין פסול מכל צד, ומה טעם נאמר? ותירצו כי איסור הנתינים (לפי כמה שיטות) אינו אלא מדברי סופרים (גזירת דוד המלך), ולכן הוצרך לומר שאף הוא פסול (חק נתן).
Steinsaltz comment #3 on Horayot 4b:11.english: Regarding a convert or a *mamzer*, there is room to mention both, because a convert comes from a flawed drop (of seed), and a *mamzer* is disqualified from entering the congregation. But seemingly, a *natin* is disqualified from all sides, so what reason is there to mention him? They answered that the prohibition of *netinim* (according to several views) is only by rabbinic decree (a decree of King David), and therefore it was necessary to state that he too is disqualified (Chok Natan).

Steinsaltz comment #4 on Horayot 4b:11.hebrew:
בהרבה מקורות גרסו: זקן ושלא ראוי לבנים, כשני מקרים שונים (וכך נראה מפסק ההלכה של הרמב"ם בענין זה).

רש"י שואל: מה טעם פסולו של זה? והעיר בספר ב"ש שבמסכת סנהדרין מסביר רש"י עצמו את טעם הדבר שמי שלא היו לו בנים אין בו מדת הרחמנות הנחוצה לחבר הסנהדרין. ובלח"מ מסביר ששאלת רש"י היתה: מפני מה זקן שהיו לו בנים נפסל, אף שעכשיו אינו ראוי. ובר"ח מסביר שמי שלא היו לו בנים נמצא שלא קיים מצות פריה ורביה.

אבל היו שקראו ככתוב לפנינו, שלכאורה אין ראוי להעמיד בסנהדרין זקנים, וגדר הזמן הוא כאשר הוא זקן כל כך ששוב אינו ראוי לבנים.
Steinsaltz comment #4 on Horayot 4b:11.english:
In many sources, the reading is: 'an old man *and* one who is not fit for children,' as two different cases (and this is how the Rambam's *halakhic* ruling on this matter appears).

Rashi asks: What is the reason for his disqualification? And the book Be'er Sheva noted that in Tractate Sanhedrin, Rashi himself explains the reason that one who has no children lacks the measure of compassion necessary for a member of the Sanhedrin. And in Lechem Mishneh, it explains that Rashi's question was: Why is an old man who *had* children disqualified, even if he is now unfit (to father children)? And R. Chananel explains that one who had no children has not fulfilled the mitzvah of 'be fruitful and multiply.'

However, there were those who read it as written before us, that seemingly it is not appropriate to appoint old men to the Sanhedrin, and the definition of 'old' is when he is so old that he is no longer fit to father children.

Steinsaltz comment #4 on Horayot 4b:16.english: If the court intentionally issued a ruling to permit a prohibited matter, and the majority of the congregation acted upon their ruling unwittingly. The court is exempt from an offering because they acted intentionally, and each member of the congregation is obligated to bring a sin-offering. As stated in the Mishnah. (Rambam, Sefer Korbanot, Hilkhot Shegagot 13:6).

Steinsaltz comment #5 on Horayot 4b:11.hebrew: הורו בית דין בטעות להתיר איסור מן התורה, ולא היה שם ראש הישיבה ("מופלא שבבית דין") או שהיה אחד מהם מי שאינו ראוי להיות בסנהדרין, כגון גר או ממזר או זקן או מי שלא היו לו בנים (נראה שזו היתה גרסת הרמב"ם. לח"מ). וכיוצא בהם — אין זו הוראה, ובית דין פטורים, והעושים על פיהם חייבים להביא חטאת. כסתם משנה. (רמב"ם ספר קרבנות הלכות שגגות פי"ג ה"א).
Steinsaltz comment #5 on Horayot 4b:11.english: If the court erred in ruling to permit a Torah prohibition, and the head of the *yeshiva* ('most distinguished member of the court') was not present, or if one of them was unfit to be in the Sanhedrin, such as a convert, a *mamzer*, an old man, or one who had no children (it appears this was the Rambam's version, Lechem Mishneh), and similar cases — this is not a valid ruling, and the court is exempt, while those who acted upon their ruling are liable to bring a sin-offering. This is like the anonymous Mishnah (Rambam, *Sefer Korbanot*, *Hilkhot Shegagot* 13:1).

Steinsaltz comment #5 on Horayot 4b:16.english: If the court issued a ruling unwittingly, and the congregation knew that they were mistaken and nevertheless acted upon their ruling, then everyone is exempt from an offering. Since the congregation did not act based on the court's ruling, they are considered intentional and are not obligated to bring an offering, and the court is exempt because the congregation did not rely on their ruling. (Rambam, Sefer Korbanot, Hilkhot Shegagot 13:6).

Steinsaltz on Horayot 4b:1.english: א And further regarding a court ruling that involves uprooting a mitzva. Rav Yosef asked: If the court ruled that there is no prohibition against plowing on Shabbat, what is the halakha? And the sides of the question are: Do we say: Since they agree to the entire matter, to all Shabbat prohibitions, and their ruling is only concerning plowing, this is considered like nullification of a portion and fulfillment of a portion? Or perhaps, since they are uprooting the labor of plowing entirely, this is considered like uprooting the essence of the mitzva of Shabbat?

Steinsaltz on Horayot 4b:11.english: The court issued a ruling, and one of them knew that they erred, and he said to them: "You are mistaken"; or if the most distinguished member of the court (the greatest of the Sages) was not there in the session of the Sanhedrin that decided this, or if one of them was disqualified from the Sanhedrin, such as being a convert, or a mamzer, or a natin, or an old man no longer able to father children, as all of these are not fit to serve in the Sanhedrin — this court is exempt, for this is not a complete ruling,

Steinsaltz on Horayot 4b:13.english: GEMARA. We learned in the Mishnah: Or if the mufla of the court was not there – the court is exempt. From where do we derive that this is the halakha? Rav Sheshet said, and likewise the Sage of the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught: For what reason did the Sages say in the Mishnah: If the court issued a ruling with regard to a matter with which the Sadducees agree – the judges are exempt? It is because judges of such a court are not considered fit to issue rulings, since it was incumbent upon them to learn and they did not learn. Similarly, if the mufla of the court was not there, they are also exempt, because it was incumbent upon them to learn and they did not learn.

Steinsaltz on Horayot 4b:14.english: We further learned in the Mishnah: “Assembly” is stated there and “assembly” is stated here… unless all of them are fit to issue rulings. And they ask: And there, from where do we derive that all of them are fit to issue rulings? And they answer: This is as Rav Ḥisda says, the verse states concerning the appointment of the seventy Elders by Moses: “That they may stand there with you” (Numbers 11:16), meaning that “with you” refers to those similar to you, Moses, that they should all be fit to issue rulings.

Steinsaltz on Horayot 4b:15.english: And they ask: And say that “with you” means for the Divine Presence, and the verse intends to say that they should stand together to receive the Divine Presence! Rather, Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak says: We learn that all of them must be fit to issue rulings from what the verse states concerning the judges whom Moses appointed: “And they shall judge the people at all times…and ease your burden from upon you and bear it with you” (Exodus 18:22), meaning that “with you” signifies: Similar to you.

Steinsaltz on Horayot 4b:16.english: MISHNA: If the court issued an erroneous ruling unwittingly, and the entire congregation, who relied on the court, performed a transgression unwittingly—they bring a bull, as is explained in the Torah regarding a communal sin-offering for an unknown matter. If the court was intentional, meaning they knew their ruling was incorrect, and the congregation performed a transgression unwittingly, as they believed the words of the court—the individuals bring a female lamb or a female goat, as is the law for those who sin unwittingly. If the court was unwitting and erred, and the congregation performed a transgression intentionally, meaning they knew the court erred but still acted—these are exempt.

Steinsaltz on Horayot 4b:17.english: GEMARA: We learned in the Mishna: If the court issued an erroneous ruling unwittingly and the congregation performed a transgression intentionally, these are exempt. And we infer from here: But if one erred unwittingly in a manner similar to an intentional act, he is liable for a sin-offering. And what exactly were the circumstances? Where the court ruled that forbidden fat is permitted, and the one who sinned confused the forbidden fat with permitted fat, thinking that the fat before him was permitted fat, and he ate it.

Steinsaltz on Horayot 4b:18.english: If so, let us say from here: Resolve this dilemma that Rami bar Ḥama asked (on page 2a) concerning this matter, and his question remained unresolved! And they reject this: He could say to you that this is not proof, for because the *tanna* taught in the first clause: Intentionally and acted unwittingly, the *tanna* taught in the latter clause: Unwittingly and acted intentionally, but one cannot infer anything from here.

Steinsaltz on Horayot 4b:19.english: **MISHNA:** If the judges of **the court issued a ruling and the entire congregation or a majority thereof performed on its basis** - **they bring a bull** for atonement. **And** if this error **involved idol worship** - **they bring a bull and a goat,** as explained in the Torah (Numbers 15:24); these are **the words of Rabbi Meir. Rabbi Yehuda says: It is not the court that brings an offering, but the public. If twelve tribes sinned** - **they bring twelve bulls,** as each tribe is a congregation unto itself. **And for idol worship** - **they bring twelve bulls and twelve goats;**

Steinsaltz on Horayot 4b:7.hebrew: אמרי [אומרים] בדחיית אותה ראיה: השתחויה נמי כדשנין [גם כן יש לומר כמו שתירצנו מקודם] שהתירו רק בהשתחוויה מעטה, ולא עקרו את כל האיסור.

Steinsaltz on Horayot 4b:8.hebrew: ועוד בענין הוראת בית דין שיש בה עקירת מצוה. בעי [שאל] ר' זירא: הורו בית הדין שאין איסור שבת בשנה השביעית (שנת השמיטה), מהו? ולפני שמבררים את השאלה, מקדימים ושואלים: במאי [במה] טעו, מה גרם להם לטעות זו? בהדין קרא [בפסוק זה] שנאמר במצות השבת: "בחריש ובקציר תשבת" (שמות לד, כא), והם מפרשים: בזמן דאיכא [שיש] חרישה כלומר, בשאר השנים איכא [יש] איסור שבת, ובזמן דליכא [שאין] חרישה בשנת השמיטה, שאסור לחרוש בה ליכא [אין] איסור שבת נוהג.

Steinsaltz on Horayot 5a:1.english: **Rabbi Shimon says: They bring thirteen bulls,** which are one bull for each and every tribe and one bull for the court. **And for idol worship** - **thirteen bulls and thirteen goats,** which are **a bull and a goat for each and every tribe,** and another **bull and a goat for the court.**

Steinsaltz on Horayot 5a:2.english: **If the court issued a ruling and seven tribes or a majority thereof performed on its basis** - **they bring a bull. And for idol worship** - **they bring a bull and a goat; these are the words of Rabbi Meir. Rabbi Yehuda says: Seven tribes that sinned** - **they bring seven bulls,** as each tribe brings an offering. **And the rest of the tribes that did not sin** - they too **bring on their behalf** (because of the sinners) **a bull** for each tribe, **for even these who did not sin bring on behalf of the sinners. Rabbi Shimon says:** When seven tribes sinned - they bring only **eight bulls,** which are seven bulls for the tribes that sinned and another one for the court. **And for idol worship** - **eight bulls and eight goats,** which are **a bull and a goat for each and every tribe,** and another **bull and a goat for the court.**

Steinsaltz on Horayot 5a:3.english: **If the court of one of the tribes issued a ruling,** which was a general court for that tribe, **and that tribe performed on its basis** - **that tribe is liable, and the rest of all the tribes are exempt; these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda. And the Rabbis say: They are liable** to bring a communal unwitting sin-offering **only for rulings of the High Court alone, as it is stated: “And if the entire assembly of Israel shall act unwittingly”** (Leviticus 4:13), to teach us: specifically the court ("assembly") of all Israel, **and not the assembly** (court) of **that** individual **tribe,** for that is not the assembly of all Israel.

Tosafot on Horayot 4b:11:1.hebrew: או שלא היה מופלא שבב"ד שם - פרש"י: ולא היה במנין, דאילו כן, אפילו קטן שבהם נמי כדאמרינן לעיל שיהיו כולן בהוראה. וקשה: דהא אתותב לעיל (נ"ל דצריכין לומר דלפני התו' לא היה כתוב לעיל הא דמסיק ואלא מאי כל עדת דקאמר רחמנא כו' עי' לקמן ברש"י דף (ה') [הוריות ז'] ע"א) ובתורת כהנים מוסיף נמי: אם אמר אחד 'איני יודע', דכמאן דליתיה דמיא:
Tosafot on Horayot 4b:11:1.english: Or if the most distinguished member of the court was not there - Rashi explains: He was not part of the quorum, for if so, even the youngest among them also (being absent) would mean, as we said above, that all of them must be present for a ruling. And it is difficult: For it was refuted above (it seems necessary to say that before Tosafot, what is concluded above was not written, 'but what does the Merciful One mean by "the entire assembly," etc.' See below in Rashi, page (5) [Horayot 7a]) and in Torat Kohanim it also adds: If one said 'I do not know,' it is as if he is not present.

Tosafot on Horayot 4b:11:2.hebrew: אחד מהן גר או ממזר - בירושלמי: שעברו ומנוהו. דמי שאין ראוי להוראה נעשה כאבן:
Tosafot on Horayot 4b:11:2.english: One of them was a convert or a mamzer - In the Yerushalmi: They transgressed and appointed him. For one who is not fit to issue rulings becomes like a stone.

Tosafot on Horayot 4b:1:1.hebrew: בעי רב יוסף אין חרישה וכולי - רישא דאבות מלאכות דפרק כלל גדול נקט, אבל חרישה צדוקין מודין בה. ולרב יוסף נמי בעי דבר שאין מודין בו, כדלקמן אמר לך רב יוסף וכולי, משמע דסבר כשמואל:

Tosafot on Horayot 4b:8:1.hebrew: שמע מינה אין שבת בשביעית וכולי - משמע דאין צדוקין מודין בהאי דרשא, אף על גב דלעיל דרשי ליה יהיה לה לשומרת (יבם) [יום]:
